title: Dualizable ordinary derived modules are precisely perfect complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and equip its ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ and unit $A[0]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, applied on the one-object site with the identity covering]. An object $Q\in D(A)$ is dualizable, meaning that there exist $Q^\vee\in D(A)$ and maps $Q^\vee\otimes_A^L Q\to A[0]$ and $A[0]\to Q\otimes_A^L Q^\vee$ satisfying both triangle identities, if and only if $Q$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], that is, isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules. No Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Suppose $Q$ is perfect. Choose $P^\bullet\simeq Q$ bounded with finite-projective terms by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Apply [lem-zl-bounded-projective-complex-dual-pairing] to obtain its bounded finite-projective dual $D$, evaluation and coevaluation at the level of complexes. Every term of $P,D$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], and both complexes, as well as $A[0]$, are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. On the one-object site, [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies their total tensors with derived tensors, naturally in the chain maps. Thus their evaluation and coevaluation localize to maps in $D(A)$ with the same two triangle identities: applying the functor $Q$ to each chain identity preserves composition and identities, and the tensor comparisons are the ones defining derived tensor. Conjugate the maps by the chosen isomorphism $Q\simeq P$ (and its inverse); the adjacent inverse composites cancel in each triangle. This proves dualizability of $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0FNS, lemma-have-dual-derived, first paragraph; Tag 0FNK, lemma-left-dual-complex

proof.text: Conversely take a dual $N$ of $Q$ with $\eta:A[0]\to Q\otimes_A^L N$ and $\epsilon:N\otimes_A^L Q\to A[0]$. Choose any complex $M$ representing $Q$. On the one-object site, [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a representative $V$ of $N$ which is K-flat and has flat terms. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to the identity ring map and the first factor $V$: using the symmetry of derived and ordinary total tensor, it computes $Q\otimes_A^L N$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_A V)$, naturally in $M$. By [lem-pc-derived-free-module-hom-homology], $\eta$ corresponds to a class in $H^0$ of that total complex. Choose a degree-zero cycle $z$ in this class. The chain map $A[0]\to\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_A V)$ sending $1$ to $z$ represents $\eta$: its class under the stated natural Hom--cohomology equivalence is precisely $[z]$.

source.place: Tag 0FNS, converse, choice of representatives and chain representative of the coevaluation

proof.text: By the direct-sum total tensor formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], write $z=\sum_{n,j}m_{n,j}\otimes v_{-n,j}$ with finitely many summands. Let $K^n\subset M^n$ be generated by all the $m_{n,j}$ in degree $n$ and all $d_M(m_{n-1,j})$. Since $d_M^2=0$, this is a subcomplex. It is zero outside a finite interval. Apply the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with flat module $V^q$ to the exact sequence $0\to K^p\to M^p$. Each $K^p\otimes V^q\to M^p\otimes V^q$ is injective; hence the total inclusion is degreewise injective. The same expression $z$ has a preimage $\widetilde z$ in $\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes V)^0$, and its differential is zero by injectivity in degree $1$. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], this chain map represents $\widetilde\eta:A[0]\to K\otimes_A^L N$ and its composite along $i:K\to Q$ is $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0FNS, converse, finite-support subcomplex and lifted coevaluation

proof.text: Define $r:Q\to K$ by $Q=A[0]\otimes_A^L Q\xrightarrow{\widetilde\eta\otimes1}K\otimes_A^L N\otimes_A^L Q\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon}K$. Naturality of tensor and associators gives $i\circ r=(1_Q\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\eta\otimes1_Q)=1_Q$, the first triangle identity. The cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore make every $H^n(Q)$ a retract of $H^n(K)$. If $K^n=0$ for $n>c$, then $H^n(K)=0$ there, so $1_{H^n(Q)}=H^n(i)H^n(r)=0$. Thus $H^n(Q)=0$ for $n>c$. The good truncation $M'=(\cdots\to M^{c-1}\to\ker d_M^c\to0\to\cdots)$ maps to $M$ and induces an isomorphism on every cohomology module: below $c$ the cycles and boundaries agree, at $c$ they are $\ker d_M^c/\operatorname{im}d_M^{c-1}$, and above $c$ both cohomologies vanish. Hence $M'$ is a bounded-above representative of $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0FNS, converse, retraction diagram and deduction that the object belongs to the bounded-above derived category

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] to $M'$ in the abelian category of $A$-modules, with $\mathcal P$ the free modules and upper bound $c$. The required quotient condition holds because the free module with basis the underlying set of any module maps surjectively onto it by sending its basis vector $[x]$ to $x$; the zero module is free. We obtain a bounded-above free complex $F$ with a quasi-isomorphism to $M'$, thus representing $Q$. Keep the K-flat flat-term model $V$ of $N$. As in Step 2, the K-flat computation [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and [lem-pc-derived-free-module-hom-homology] represent $\eta$ by a degree-zero cycle $z_F=\sum_{n,j} f_{n,j}\otimes v_{-n,j}$ of $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_A V)$ with finitely many summands.

source.place: Tag 0FNS, converse, bounded-above free replacement; Tag 05T7, derived-lemma-subcategory-left-resolution

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-bounded-free-finite-subcomplex] to the finite list of all $f_{n,j}$. It gives a bounded finite-free subcomplex $G\subset F$ containing them. Applying the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with flat module $V^q$ to $0\to G^p\to F^p$ again makes $\operatorname{Tot}(G\otimes V)\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes V)$ degreewise injective, so the preimage of $z_F$ is a cycle. The natural computation [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] gives a lift $\eta_G:A[0]\to G\otimes_A^L N$ of $\eta$. Put $j:G\to Q$ for the inclusion followed by the representative isomorphism, and $s=(1_G\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\eta_G\otimes1_Q):Q\to G$. The same explicit composite as Step 4 gives $j\circ s=1_Q$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], $G$ is perfect: its terms are finite free, hence finite projective (a free module lifts along surjections by lifting each basis vector).

source.place: Tag 0FNS, final paragraph, applying Tag 0FNR and repeating the triangle-identity retraction

proof.text: Complete $s:Q\to G$ to a distinguished triangle $Q\xrightarrow{s}G\to C\xrightarrow{w}Q[1]$, as allowed by [def-weil-triangulated-category] and the derived structure [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the twice-rotated triangle. It gives $s[1]\circ w=0$ (the rotation sign does not affect vanishing). Since $j\circ s=1_Q$, shifting gives $j[1]\circ s[1]=1_{Q[1]}$, and hence $w=j[1]s[1]w=0$. Therefore [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split] gives $G\simeq Q\oplus C$. Perfectness is invariant under isomorphism directly from [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], so $Q\oplus C$ is perfect. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-ring-summand] to conclude that $Q$ is perfect. Every construction used the given commutative ring only, without Noetherianity or $1\ne0$.

lean.statement: theorem dualizable_iff_isPerfectRingComplex {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (Q : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) : (∃ (D : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (ev : D ⊗ Q ⟶ 𝟙_ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))) (coev : 𝟙_ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) ⟶ Q ⊗ D), (λ_ Q).inv ≫ coev ▷ Q ≫ (α_ Q D Q).hom ≫ Q ◁ ev ≫ (ρ_ Q).hom = 𝟙 Q ∧ (ρ_ D).inv ≫ D ◁ coev ≫ (α_ D Q D).inv ≫ ev ▷ D ≫ (λ_ D).hom = 𝟙 D) ↔ IsPerfectRingComplex Q
